# Ogus, the Baboon

Ogus the baboon sits in the center of it all,  
chained to a post between the small house and back stoop,  
where with wary eyes he watches the comings and goings on the yard:  
the proud tom turkey displaying his pompous tail;  
the dog barking at its own tail, howling to the moon at night;  
the hen that scuttles, hiding her chicks beneath the tractor's shade—  
yet his greatest ire is reserved for the owner of this place,  
who, at the crack of dawn, drives all that lives and breathes from you:  
"What mischief have you gotten into now, do you struggle to understand?  
You seem as foolish as that ole baboon."
